'''Brian Foster''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRS|OBE|HonFInstP}} (born 4 January 1954 in [[Roddymoor]], [[Crook, County Durham|Crook]], Co. Durham) is a British experimental particle physicist. He is Donald H. Perkins Professor of Experimental Physics Emeritus at the department of physics, [[University of Oxford]],<ref name="RS"/><ref name="University of Oxford Department of Physics 2011">{{cite web | title=Brian Foster | website=University of Oxford Department of Physics | date=24 February 2011 | url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/fosterb | access-date=17 March 2019}}</ref> and  [[Alexander von Humboldt Professor]] a. D. at the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref name="Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESY">{{cite web | title=Brian Foster | website=Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESY | url=http://www.desy.de/about_desy/lead_scientists/brian_foster/index_eng.html | access-date=18 March 2019 | archive-date=23 April 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423170257/http://www.desy.de/about_desy/lead_scientists/brian_foster/index_eng.html | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="DESY 2019">{{cite web | title=Humboldt Professur – Alexander von Humboldt-Professor Dr. Brian Foster FRS | website=DESY | date=12 March 2019 | url=https://humboldt-professur.desy.de/ | access-date=18 March 2019}}</ref> He was leading scientist at [[DESY]] where his research topics include new methods of acceleration, [[deep inelastic scattering]] using the [[ZEUS]] particle detector, and the [[International Linear Collider]].<ref name="DESY 2019"/> He began his career on the 4,2m bubble chamber at [[CERN]] and then became a postdoctoral researcher at [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] and [[Imperial College London]], where he worked on the [[TASSO]] experiment at [[DESY]]. He was an author of the paper in which the discovery of the [[gluon]] was announced.<ref name="gluon">{{cite web | title=Evidence for Planar Events in e+e− Annihilation at High Energies| website=Physics Letters| date=24 September 1979 | url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/037026937990830X | access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref> He spent 20 years at [[Bristol University]] as successively Lecturer, Reader and then Professor of Experimental physics and head of the particle physics group. He was a member of the [[BaBar collaboration]] that discovered CP-violation in the B-quark system.<ref name="CPviolation">{{cite web | title=Observation of 𝐶𝑃 Violation in the 𝐵0 Meson System| website=Physical Review Letters| date=14 August 2001 | url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.091801 | access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref> He then became head of particle physics at [[Oxford University]] and a Fellow of [[Balliol College Oxford]]. In the last 20 years, Foster has worked predominantly in [[accelerator physics]], particularly [[plasma acceleration]]. In 2004, he founded the [[John Adams Institute for Accelerator Science]], a joint venture initially between [[Oxford University]] and [[Royal Holloway, University of London]], subsequently joined by [[Imperial College London]]. He conceived the HALHF project,<ref name="HALHF">{{cite web | title=A hybrid, asymmetric, linear Higgs factory based on plasma-wakefield and radio-frequency acceleration| website=New Journal of Physics| date=21 September 2023 | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/acf395 | access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref> to design a much cheaper, greener form of Higgs Factory based on a hybrid of plasma- and conventional-based acceleration. His biography of Einstein, "Einstein - A Life in Science and Music" <ref name="ELSM">{{cite web | title=Einstein - A Life in Science and Music| website=Oxford University Press| date=4 February 2026 | url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/einstein-a-life-in-science-and-music-9780198794875?cc=pt&lang=en& | access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref> was published by Oxford University Press in February 2026.

==Music==
{{unreferencedsect|date=October 2026}}
Foster is an amateur violinist, who uses the instrument to help elucidate concepts in physics in popular lectures. Together with virtuoso violinist [[Jack Liebeck]], he devised the ''Superstrings'' and ''Einstein's Universe'' lectures which link Einstein's love of music, his science and the latest discoveries in particle physics. They have been delivered world-wide around 200 times to live audiences totalling around 30,000. He has organised commissions of new works by [[Emily Hall]] and [[Anna Meredith]], and by [[Edward Cowie]]. Foster is Vice President of the International Ernest Bloch Society. He and [[Jack Liebeck]] founded the Oxford May Music Festival in 2007, which combines cutting-edge science events with world-class concerts.

==Honours and awards==

Foster was awarded a [[Humboldt Research Award]] in 1998 and both the [[Max Born Prize]] and the [[Order of the British Empire]] in 2003. He was selected for an [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship]] in 2011.<ref name="Alexander von Humboldt-Professur">{{cite web | title=Brian Foster | website=Alexander von Humboldt-Professur | url=https://www.humboldt-professur.de/de/preistraeger/preistraeger-2011/foster-brian | language=de | access-date=18 March 2019 | archive-date=13 February 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213021813/http://www.humboldt-professur.de/de/preistraeger/preistraeger-2011/foster-brian | url-status=dead }}</ref> Foster was elected to the [[Royal Society]] in 2008.<ref name="RS">{{cite web | title=Brian Foster | website=Royal Society | date=19 September 2015 | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/brian-foster-11451/ | access-date=17 March 2019}}</ref> He served as a vice-president of the [[Royal Society]] in 2018 and was elected Honorary Fellow of the UK [[Institute of Physics]] in 2020.<ref name="IoP">{{cite web | title=Brian Foster | website=Institute of Physics | date=2020 | url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/honorary-fellowship/our-honorary-fellows/professor-brian-foster | access-date=26 April 2022}}</ref>

==Publications==

Books

1.	B.Foster, editor, “Topics in High Energy Particle Physics”,
Institute of Physics Publishing Ltd., 1988. 152pp.

2.	B.Foster  and P.H.Fowler, editors, “40 Years of Particle Physics”,
Adam Hilger, 1988. 261 pp.

3.	B.Foster, editor, “Electron-Positron Annihilation Physics”,
Adam Hilger, 1990. 231 pp.

4. B. Foster, "Einstein - A Life in Science and Music", 
Oxford University Press, 2026. 684 pp.

Books (translation)

H.V. Klapdor-Kleingrothaus and K. Zuber, “Particle Astrophysics”,
Institute of Physics Publishing Ltd., 1997. 507 pp. (From original German,
with S.M. Foster)

Articles

Over 650 articles in refereed journals, including ''Nature, Nature Communications, Physics Letters'', ''Physical Review Letters'' and ''European Journal of English Studies''.
